title.value: Gradient Starvation: A Learning Proclivity in Neural Networks
title.justification: This title encapsulates the primary focus of the paper, which is on the phenomenon of Gradient Starvation and its effects on learning in neural networks.
title.quote: Gradient Starvation: A Learning Proclivity in Neural Networks

analysis.description: This research paper addresses the phenomenon of Gradient Starvation in neural networks, which occurs when cross-entropy loss leads neural networks to focus primarily on a subset of features, ignoring others that are also predictive. The paper provides a theoretical explanation using concepts from dynamical systems theory and proposes a regularization method called Spectral Decoupling to mitigate this issue. Empirical evaluations on classification and adversarial tasks are presented to support the theoretical findings.

type.justification: The paper provides a theoretical framework and formalizes the concept of Gradient Starvation using theoretical tools from dynamical systems and proposes a mathematical approach to mitigate it.
type.quote: This work provides a theoretical explanation for the emergence of such feature imbalances in neural networks.

name.justification: The paper deals with the behavior and training dynamics of neural networks, which are central topics in Deep Learning.
name.quote: We identify and formalize a fundamental gradient descent phenomenon leading to a learning proclivity in over-parameterized neural networks.

name.justification: The paper is primarily concerned with the optimization dynamics of neural networks, particularly the phenomenon of Gradient Starvation during training.
name.quote: Using perturbation analysis, we formalize Gradient Starvation (GS) in view of the coupling between the dynamics of orthogonal directions in the feature space (Thm. 2).

name.justification: The paper includes empirical results on adversarial attack tasks and discusses the robustness implications of Gradient Starvation.
name.quote: We support our findings with extensive empirical results on a variety of classification and adversarial attack tasks.

name.justification: The paper mentions using a two-layer ReLU network in its experiments to demonstrate the phenomenon.
name.quote: A two-layer ReLU network with 500 hidden units is trained with cross-entropy loss for two different arrangements of the training points.
